i.norm: Tests that StreamParser.iterator() correctly emits elements in document order when parsing an HTML fragment, and closes the reader once iteration completes.

Appends a short descriptor for {@code el} to {@code actual}:
  • tag name (e.g. "td")
  • "#id" if the element has an id attribute
  • "[text]" if the element has direct text
  • "+" if the element had a next sibling at emission time
  • ";" as a delimiter between entries
Returns true when the StreamParser has closed its underlying CharacterReader, which happens automatically once all input has been consumed.
Fragment HTML with a missing </tr> — the parser infers it when the next <tr> begins.
Parse within a <table> context so the browser-like fragment rules apply.
Consume every element emitted by the iterator and record its descriptor.

Expected emission order (children before parents; "+" means a next sibling existed at emission time). Note: we receive the fragment elements plus the context element at the top of the stack, not a full document.
Exhausting the iterator must close the underlying reader automatically.
